I agreed because we're willing to pay anything for our animals. After the X-ray, they told me the "clinic" doesn't handle that kind of procedure (a pin in a broken leg), but I still owed 160 euros. Yes, thankfully, the Massilia clinic in the 12th arrondissement. Everything else is just quackery or a scam.

I made an appointment on April 2nd to vaccinate my 3-month-old cat with Mr. Jean-Luc Bernheim.
I arrived, everything seemed fine, he saw my cat, and I told him that my cat is active and doesn't cooperate.
The vaccination went well, but when it came time to give him the deworming pill, my cat resisted and scratched him (which I think is normal because he doesn't like being picked up or held). The vet didn't like that my cat wouldn't cooperate, so he slapped him. A slap from an adult to a 3-month-old kitten!
I find this UNACCEPTABLE, especially since he didn't even apologize. I was so shocked that I couldn't say anything; I was frozen.

In short, be careful who you go to, especially if it's your pet! I will never go back to your vet, and I strongly advise against this vet.

I had a consultation today for my cat, who seems to have a minor case of idiopathic cystitis, probably related to temporary stress. To begin with, we were seen 35 minutes late. Then, the vet explained the various procedures she wanted to perform, including a cost of up to €340 for an X-ray and urinalysis, which she recommended to rule out bacterial cystitis or stones. Convinced it was more likely a minor case of cystitis due to temporary stress, I finally agreed with the vet to proceed gradually. A simple blood test to start, to check if his kidneys were functioning well enough to prescribe an initial antispasmodic and anti-inflammatory treatment, after which I could return if further tests were needed. I was okay with the already high quote of 146 euros that I was given (100 euros for the blood test and consultation, and 46 euros for the medication), but when I went to the till an hour and a half later, I discovered that I had been charged an additional 51 euros for sedating the cat, which was necessary to perform the blood test. Firstly, this is the first time in 10 years that a vet has been unable to give this cat an injection (despite her annual vaccinations) and has mentioned the need to sedate her. I offered to hold her during the injection since I had managed to calm her down, but the vet told me it was better to sedate her, which I accepted, trusting her professional opinion, but without being informed that it cost an extra 51 euros! Total consultation time: 1 hour 30 minutes of waiting and €197 for a blood test and a treatment consisting of two medications. I expressed my astonishment to the veterinarian regarding the lack of information about the cost of sedation, but no attempt at negotiation was offered. I will not be returning to this clinic, which I do not recommend. I had already been several times since moving to the neighborhood, but billing for procedures (and not necessarily essential ones initially, such as X-rays and urinalysis, which can wait 8 days to see the progress of the first treatment, provided there is no blood in the urine and the cat has urinated normally for the past two days) seems clearly more important than patient retention. It's a real shame that some veterinarians prioritize profit above all else.

As a long-time client (if I may call it that), I remember this clinic being wonderful: welcoming, understanding, and humane. Mr. Lafay, Ms. Genais, and the assistants... yes, things have certainly changed. My problem was that I was waiting for my new credit card and only had my checkbook to pay. They categorically refused to accept checks without any attempt to understand that my pet was sick and needed care. I understand perfectly well that they no longer accept checks; they're not the only ones. But as a long-time client, they could have made an effort this time. It was the way they handled it that disappointed me so much, because I was worried about my pet. For some professionals, it's truly a profession of faith; for others, it's not. Avoid them at all costs.

That's what I did...
